title: Container Bookings: counting the destination changes that still owe a fee
content:
## Rule
Under the Container Bookings product line, the changes of port of discharge still owing a change-of-destination fee are counted from the booking's own ledger: the number of amendment log entries on the booking marked as a change of port of discharge, less the number of change-of-destination fee entries on the booking. When no change is still owing a fee, nothing is charged.

## Input, judgement, output
| Destination changes logged on the booking | Change-of-destination fee entries on the booking | Changes still owing a fee | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0 | 1 | a fee is due |
| 2 | 1 | 1 | a fee is due |
| 2 | 2 | 0 | nothing is charged |
| 0 | 0 | 0 | nothing is charged |

*The counts above are hypothetical inputs, for illustration only.*

## Points of judgement
**Which records are counted?** Only entries on this booking: its logged changes of port of discharge and its change-of-destination fee entries. Other amendment kinds, such as an equipment change, are not part of this count.

**The customer says the fee was paid when the change was made, but no fee entry exists on the booking.** The count is taken from the booking's ledger, not from the customer's account of events; with no fee entry, the change is still owing.
